pie: sóh₂wl̥ gʷʰréh₁yet poh₂imḗn-kʷe h₁suménēs kósloy Hn̥dʰér légʰt. swépnos h₁ím kapyét h₂óweyes-kʷe h₃slidʰént. h₁yód bʰéwdʰt h₁íh₂n̥s ne kʷéḱt. troméyet dusméneses h₁íh₂n̥s stéh₂yōnti. h₁íh₂n̥s kl̥Héni wédni-kʷe h₂isḱét. h₁ésyo ḱwṓ h₁ím sékʷeto. ḱwṓ h₂ówins séh₂gyet h₁íh₂n̥s-kʷe widét. h₁suménēs tā́s ǵʰórtom h₁n̥dó h₁élh₂t. mléwHt kósloy Hn̥dʰér h₂ew ne sésoh₂.
english: The sun was warm, and the shepherd Kindly lay down under a hazel. Sleep held him, and the sheep went astray. When he woke up, he did not see them. He trembled: "The hostile ones will steal them!" He sought them on the hill and by the water. His dog was following him. The dog tracked the sheep and found them. Kindly drove them into the enclosure. He said: "I shall not sleep under the hazel again."

pie: h₂nḗr kénket légʰyet-kʷe. dh₂pnóm súpniyoy kʷéḱt. pékʷtōr péyskm̥ pékʷet h₂ōwyéh₂-kʷe yéset. h₁ḗdt píph₃et-kʷe séh₂t-kʷe. nu bʰéwdʰt h₂ew-kʷe kénket. wéwket súpniyom me h₂élet méne ǵʰórneh₂ ne pléh₁t. nu wódr̥ h₁r̥sḱét péyskm̥-kʷe tn̥tlóh₁ h₁épt. h₁ím pékʷet h₂éḱh₃t-kʷe térpt-kʷe.
english: A man was hungry, and he was lying down. In a dream he caught sight of a feast. A cook was cooking fish, and eggs were boiling. He was eating and drinking, and he became sated. Then he woke up, and he was hungry again. He said: "The dream was nourishing me, but my gut did not become full." Then he went to the water and seized a fish with a net. He cooked it and ate it up, and he was sated.

pie: ḱwṓ poh₂imnéy h₁ést. nékʷti swépnoy h₁ést ḱwṓ ń̥supnos h₁ést. ḱl̥néwt h₂ḱh₂owsyét-kʷe. sérponts wĺ̥kʷos h₂ówins próti gʷm̥sḱét. HréwdHt h₁ím-kʷe próti drémt. poh₂imḗn bʰéwdʰt ḱéntrom-kʷe sléh₂gʷt. wĺ̥kʷos h₂epó bʰéwgt. h₁ésmey wéwket ḱéywe ḱwón túH méne péh₂tōr. h₁yód sésmi bʰéwdʰesi. h₁ésmey smérum péyskm̥-kʷe déh₃t ḱwṓ-kʷe h₁ésyo ǵʰésorm̥ léyǵʰt.
english: A shepherd had a dog. At night he was in sleep, but the dog was sleepless. It was listening, and it heard well. A wolf was coming, creeping toward the sheep. It cried out and ran at it. The shepherd woke up and seized a pointed tool. The wolf fled away. He said to it: "Dear dog, you are my guardian. When I sleep, you are awake." He gave it grease and fish, and the dog licked his hand.

pie: h₃rḗǵs h₁wesuḱléwesm̥ ǵʰórtoy kapyét. péh₂tōr h₁ím nékʷti spéḱyet. h₁wesuḱléwēs pérkʷunōy kh₂nét pérkʷune me spr̥dʰí. nu pérkʷunos péh₂torm̥ swopéyet. swépnos h₁ím sléh₂gʷt dʰǵʰémi-kʷe légʰet. h₁wesuḱléwēs ǵʰórtom Hrunépt bʰéwgt-kʷe. péh₂tōr h₂usési bʰéwdʰt gʰóstis-kʷe néḱt. h₃rḗǵs gʰrémet péh₂tōr sokʷéyet. deywós me swopéyet. deywóm kʷis próti ne memógʰe. nu h₃rḗǵs h₁ím léh₁t.
english: A king was holding Of-Goodly-Fame in an enclosure. A guardian was watching him by night. Of-Goodly-Fame chanted to Perkʷunos: "Perkʷunos, free me!" Then Perkʷunos put the guardian to sleep. Sleep took him, and he lay on the earth. Of-Goodly-Fame broke the enclosure and fled. At dawn the guardian woke up, and the stranger had vanished. The king was angry, but the guardian said: "A god put me to sleep. No one has power against a god." Then the king let him go.

pie: dusménēs deywós h₃réǵm̥ próti gʰrémet. h₁ésmey súpniyom nékʷti h₁opéyet. súpniyom h₁ésmey bʰéh₂t sth₂dʰí. márkons toy yugdʰí dusménesn̥s-kʷe h₁l̥h₂dʰí. h₁íns wénesi. bʰéwdʰt márkons yugmé h₁íns-kʷe próti h₁élh₂t. dusméneses polh₁éwes h₁sént h₁ím-kʷe unént. bʰéwgt sékʷt-kʷe súpniyoh₁ me dʰréwgʰt. h₂néres súpniyeh₂ mē sékʷedʰwe.
english: The Ill-Minded god was angry against the king. By night he gave him a dream. The dream spoke to him: "Stand up! Yoke your horses and drive to the hostile ones. You will overpower them." He woke up; he yoked the horses and drove against them. But the hostile ones were many, and they overpowered him. He fled and said: "He deceived me with a dream." Men, do not follow dreams!

pie: swépnos mr̥téys bʰréh₂tēr. swépnos h₂nérn̥s nékʷti gʷm̥sḱéti. h₁íns kapyéti h₁íns-kʷe moḱs léh₁t. mértis h₁íns h₁r̥h₁pyéti ne-kʷe séh₁t. polh₁uh₁éḱwos supnóy h₂éǵroy h₁ést. swépnos mértis-kʷe h₁ím gʷm̥sḱétām. mértis bʰéh₂t bʰréh₂ter ḱóm sléh₂gʷoh₂. swépnos h₂éǵt h₁ím mē sléh₂gʷs h₁ím tetólh₂h₂e. h₁yód h₂wésm̥ polh₁uh₁éḱwos h₁gért h₂epó-kʷe h₁r̥sḱét. mértis léytt h₂ew gʷm̥yḗti. h₁éy h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr. h₂néres h₁ím gʷr̥nHté léh₁t wos.
english: Sleep is the brother of Death. By night Sleep comes to men. He grasps them, and early he lets them go. Death seizes them and does not let them go. Of-Many-Horses was in sleep in the field. Sleep and Death were coming to him. Death said: "Brother, let me take this one." Sleep said: "Do not take him; I am holding him up." When it grew bright, Of-Many-Horses woke up and went away. Death went away, but she will come again. He is the giver of good things. Men, praise him: he lets you go!

pie: h₁suwékʷēs h₂éǵrom h₂érh₃yet. ḱémh₂t légʰt-kʷe nókʷts-kʷe h₁ím swopéyet. bʰéwdʰt h₂éboles h₁rudʰéh₁n̥t pékʷonto-kʷe. yugóm Hrumptó swṓs-kʷe gʷówes h₃slidʰént. ḱóymom yéh₂t h₁ím-kʷe ne ǵn̥nh₃ént. wr̥h₁ént kʷís ḱós h₁ésti? h₁ésyo pótnih₂ h₁nédʰt h₁ím-kʷe ǵnéh₃t. h₂éǵt kúdʰe wíHre h₁és? h₂éboles dwís pékʷonto. dʰémbʰt méǵh₂s swépnos.
english: Of-Good-Speech was ploughing a field. He became tired and lay down, and the Night put him to sleep. He woke up: the apples were red, and they were ripening. The yoke had broken, and his own cattle had gone astray. He was going to the village, and they did not recognize him. They said: "Who is this?" His wife came forth, and she knew him. She said: "Husband, where were you? Twice the apples have ripened!" He was astonished: "Great is sleep!"

pie: pótnih₂ septḿ̥ h₂éboln̥s swópniyoy widét h₁yóy swéh₂h₁ ǵʰésorh₁e h₁n̥dó sn̥gʷént. h₁wesuménesey h₁íd sokʷéyet. h₁wesuménēs h₁íd déyḱet septḿ̥ h₂éboles septḿ̥ suHnéwes. septḿ̥ toy suHnéwes ǵn̥h₁yṓntor h₁éysōm-kʷe h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm h₁éseti. h₁ésyeh₂ey-kʷe ǵn̥h₁yónto. h₂uksént Hyudʰsmṓs-kʷe bʰuHént. septḿ̥-kʷe Hyudʰsmṓm méh₂term̥ gʷr̥nHént.
english: In a dream a wife saw seven apples, which fell into her hands. She told it to Of-Good-Mind. Of-Good-Mind pointed it out: "The seven apples are seven sons. Seven sons will be born to you, and their name will be famous." And they were born to her. They grew up and became warriors. And they praised the mother of the seven warriors.

pie: dwóyh₁ dʰugh₂térh₁e nékʷti troméyetām. sokʷéyetām. kʷíd méh₂ter nókʷts gʷm̥sḱéti? trésowos. sékʷt méne príHeh₂h₁ mē tr̥mtóm. nókʷts h₂usés swésōr. dʰéǵʰōm woséyeti h₂óweyes-kʷe swépnoy ḱéyror. nu h₂éwsōs diwés dʰugh₂tḗr mélh₃t bʰudʰént-kʷe. ne dʰrugʰyéti h₁yóy ssénti tóns h₂lékseti. nu légʰyetām swépnos-kʷe h₁íh₂n̥s sléh₂gʷt.
english: Two daughters were trembling at night. They said: "Mother, why does the night come? We are trembling." She said: "Do not tremble, my dear ones. Night is the sister of Dawn. She clothes the earth, and the sheep lie in sleep. Then Dawn, the daughter of Sky, comes forth, and they wake up. She does not deceive; she protects those who sleep." Then they were lying down, and sleep took them.

pie: Hyudʰsmósyo pótnih₂ swópniyom nékʷti widéh₁yet. h₁ógʷʰis swóy démi légʰet. bʰéyh₂t h₁yéh₂-kʷe wóyde tā́m h₁r̥sḱét. mléwHt. méh₂ter h₁ógʷʰim swépnoy méne démi widóm. kʷíd swópniyom wérh₁yeti? h₁suménēs h₁íd déyḱet. dʰúgh₂ter mē bʰéyh₂s. h₁ógʷʰis ḱóymosyo péh₂tōr. suHnús toy ǵn̥h₁yḗtor h₁ím-kʷe h₂léksēti. h₁ésyeh₂ey-kʷe ǵn̥h₁yéto. h₁ógʷʰis ph₂wéni h₂énti ḱéyo h₂wékst-kʷe kéh₂ilos-kʷe h₁ést. pótnih₂ h₁suménesey h₂l̥h₁wéns médos déh₃t.
english: The wife of a warrior was seeing a dream at night. A snake was lying in her own house. She became afraid, and she went to her who knows. She said: "Mother, in my sleep I saw a snake in my house. What does the dream say?" The Kindly One pointed it out: "Do not be afraid, daughter. The snake is the guardian of the household. A son will be born to you, and it will protect him." And he was born to her. The snake lay near the fire, and he grew up and was healthy. The wife gave the Kindly One a measure of flour.

pie: ǵʰwḗr ḱóymom gʷm̥sḱét h₂ówins-kʷe gʷr̥h₃ét. wiHrṓs trésont h₁éǵʰs-kʷe kʷis ne h₁éyt. nu Hyudʰsmós deywóǵenh₁ēs mléwHt ḱósyeh₂i kʷsépi ne sésoh₂. tn̥tlóh₁ h₂éwisu h₂énti sédyet bʰéwdʰet-kʷe. sérponts ǵʰwḗr nékʷti gʷémt. tn̥tlóm h₁ésmi upér Hyéh₁kt h₁ím-kʷe gʷʰént. h₁yód h₂wést wiHrṓs ǵʰwḗrm̥ kʷḱént Hyudʰsmóm-kʷe gʷr̥nHént. ń̥supnos h₁és nu-kʷe ssmés. h₁ím déront.
english: A beast was coming to the village, and it was devouring the sheep. The men were trembling, and no one went out. Then the warrior Of-Divine-Race said: "I shall not sleep this night." He sat by the sheep with a net, and he was awake. In the night the beast came creeping. He threw the net over it and struck it down. When it grew bright, the men caught sight of the beast, and they praised the warrior: "You were sleepless, and now we sleep." They were flaying it.

pie: poh₂imḗn h₁wesuḱléwēs wĺ̥kʷom súpniyoy widét. h₁ésyo gʷṓs h₂éḱh₃t. h₁yéh₂ wóyde tā́m gʷéh₂t h₁ésyeh₂ey-kʷe súpniyom wérh₁yet. mléwHt wĺ̥kʷos gʷoldʰós gʷoldʰós gʷm̥yḗti. h₂léh₁wr̥ h₁n̥dóm dʰh₁dʰí. h₂léh₁wr̥ h₁n̥dóm dʰéh₁t. nu dʰéǵʰōm térst gʷoldʰós-kʷe ḱóymom h₁ért. kénkont h₁wesuḱléwēs h₁éymos h₂léh₁wr̥ déh₃t. h₁ésyo ḱléwos méǵh₂ bʰúHt.
english: The herdsman Of-Goodly-Fame saw a wolf in a dream. It ate up his cattle. He went to her who knows and told her the dream. She said: "The wolf is hunger; hunger will come. Put flour inside!" He put the flour inside. Then the earth dried up, and hunger arrived in the village. They were hungry, but Of-Goodly-Fame gave them flour. His fame became great.

pie: h₃rēǵés suHnús h₁suǵénh₁ēs nókʷtm̥ wéydset. h₁ésyo méh₂tēr wérh₁yet l̥gʰdʰí. ne légʰet kl̥Héni sédyet. dyḗm spéḱyet wérteto. ǵʰwḗr sérpet h₁suǵénh₁ēs troméyet ne bʰéwgt. nu h₂wést sóh₂wl̥-kʷe mélh₃t. ní gʷémt wérh₁yet-kʷe. nókʷtm̥ h₂éwsosm̥-kʷe dedórḱe. méǵh₂ih₂ h₁ést priHéh₂ h₁ést. nu swépnos h₁ím h₁épt.
english: A king's son, Of-Good-Race, wanted to see the night. His mother said: "Lie down!" But he did not lie down; he sat on the hill. He looked at the sky; it was turning. A beast crept past; Of-Good-Race trembled, but he did not flee. Then it became bright, and the sun came forth. He came down, and he said: "I have seen the night and the dawn. It was great, but she was dear." Then sleep seized him.

pie: swésōr swóm bʰréh₂term̥ súpniyoy widéh₁yet. kl̥Héni ḱéyo ḱémh₂t-kʷe. HréwdHt swésor h₁mé gʷm̥dʰí. bʰéwdʰt wódr̥-kʷe sléh₂gʷt upó-kʷe stéygʰet. h₁ím h₂én widét h₁ím-kʷe tl̥néh₂t. h₃sléydʰt tr̥syét-kʷe. h₁ésmey h₁íd déh₃t péh₃t-kʷe gʷíh₃wet-kʷe. sékʷt kʷíh₁ swésor ǵnéh₃s? wérh₁t súpniyom me déwkt. nu h₁ésyo swésorm̥ stérgeti.
english: A sister was seeing her own brother in a dream. He was lying on a hill, and he had become tired. He cried out: "Sister, come to me!" She woke up, took water, and climbed up. There she found him, and she was lifting him up. He had gone astray, and he was thirsty. She gave it to him, and he drank and lived. He said: "Sister, how did you know?" She said: "The dream led me." Now he cherishes his sister.

pie: h₁éḱwōs tu weukʷónt, "ḱludʰí, h₂ówei, ḱḗr gʰe Hegʰnutór n̥sméi widn̥tbʰ(y)ós. Hnḗr, pótis, h₂éwyom r̥ wl̥h₂néHm sebʰi kʷr̥néuti nu gʷʰérmom wéstrom néǵʰi h₂éwyom wl̥h₂néH h₁ésti."
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: Hyudʰsmṓs démi supnóy ḱéyro. péh₂tōr bʰéwdʰet. kʷsépi ḱléwset. sérpontn̥s dusménesn̥s ḱléwt. HréwdHt Hyúdʰsmōs bʰudʰté. dusméneses gʷegʷmḗr. h₁grént swéh₂-kʷe ḱéntreh₂ h₁pént. h₁íns h₁éǵʰs h₂éǵont. h₃rḗǵs ph₂tréy wérh₁t ń̥supnos h₁és n̥smé spérs. ḱléwos toy méǵh₂ h₁syéh₁t. h₁ésmey-kʷe misdʰóm márkom déh₃t.
english: In the house the warriors were lying in sleep. But the guardian was awake. In the night he was listening. He heard the hostile ones creeping. He cried out: "Warriors, wake up! The hostile ones have come!" They woke up and seized their own pointed tools. They drove them out. The king said to the guardian: "You were sleepless; you rescued us. May your fame be great!" And he gave him a reward, a horse.

pie: dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁e gʷṓs h₂éǵroy ph₂stā́m. h₁yód h₁regʷesyét l̥gʰtā́m supnóy-kʷe h₁stā́m. gʰóstis kʷsépi h₁ludʰét h₁íns-kʷe h₂epó h₁élh₂t. h₁yód h₂wést bʰréh₂terh₁e bʰudʰtā́m. h₁suḱléwēs sékʷt bʰréh₂ter nos gʷówes lelikʷḗr. deywóǵenh₁ēs h₂éǵt tóns h₂isḱṓwos. h₁íns wódr̥ séh₂gyetām. h₁íns supnóy-kʷe ḱéym̥h₁nom gʰóstim h₂én kʷḱtā́m. tóns ḱóymom h₂éǵetām. ne h₁gért. swépnos gʷṓs h₁épt swépnos-kʷe h₁íns h₂ew déh₃t. h₁íns Hwr̥tā́m ń̥supnoh₁ pós h₁stā́m.
english: Two brothers were guarding the cattle in the field. When it was getting dark, they lay down, and they were in sleep. In the night a stranger arrived and drove them away. When it grew bright, the brothers woke up. Of-Good-Fame said: "Brother, our cattle are gone!" Of-Divine-Race said: "Let us seek them." They tracked them to the water. There they caught sight of them and the stranger, lying in sleep. They drove them home. He did not wake up. Sleep seized the cattle, and sleep gave them back. They enclosed them; afterwards they were sleepless.

pie: h₁wesuḱléwēs kʷsépi h₁éyt stéwdt-kʷe. péh₂wr̥ kʷéḱt dṓm-kʷe h₁ésmi h₂énti widét. h₁sudéh₃neh₂ h₁ésmōd h₁nédʰt wéwket-kʷe. gʰóstey wiḱdʰí h₁idʰé-kʷe sddʰí. h₁ím h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂h₁ woséyet h₁ésmey-kʷe mélit h₁áyt h₁ḗdt gʷʰért-kʷe. nu h₁ím logʰéyet supnóy-kʷe h₁ést. moḱs h₁gért kl̥Héni ḱéyo. dṓm néḱt péh₂wr̥-kʷe stéwdt. h₁ésyo ḱḗr gʷʰréh₁yet ne-kʷe kénket. sékʷt ḱód swópniyom h₁ést deywósyo-wē dṓm h₁ést. nu h₁éymn̥ h₁éyt.
english: Of-Goodly-Fame was going through the night, and he became cold. He caught sight of a fire, and near it he saw a house. Of-Good-Gifts came forth from it and said: "Guest, enter, and sit down here!" She clothed him with wool, and she gave him honey; he ate and became warm. Then she laid him down, and he was in sleep. Early he woke up: he was lying on a hill. The house had vanished, and the fire had become cold. But his heart was warm, and he was not hungry. He said: "Was this a dream, or the house of a god?" Then he was going on the way.

pie: h₁suh₁éḱwos h₂éǵrom h₁r̥sḱét kósloy-kʷe Hn̥dʰér légʰt. méǵh₂s swépnos h₁ím lémbʰt. swépnoy pl̥h₁uyéh₂su nékʷtsu légʰet. péth₂leh₂ séngʷt péth₂leh₂-kʷe h₂ew h₂wékst. nu bʰéwdʰt ḱóymom-kʷe gʷéh₂t. h₂nḗr démi sth₂éh₁yet. h₁suh₁éḱwos h₁ím ne ǵn̥néh₃t sokʷéyet-kʷe kʷís túH h₁ési? wérh₁t h₁eǵóh₂ h₁suh₁éḱwosyo suHnús. ph₂tḗr moy léytt néḱt-kʷe. nu dʰémbʰt h₂éǵt-kʷe súHnew toy h₁eǵóh₂ ph₂tḗr. méwdt h₁ím-kʷe ph₂wéni h₁épi sodéyet. sékʷt h₁eh₁lówdʰth₂e supnóy-kʷe h₁ésm̥.
english: Of-Good-Horses went to the pasture and lay down under a hazel. A great sleep seized him. He lay in sleep through many nights. The leaves fell, and the leaves grew again. Then he woke up and went home. In the house a man was standing. Of-Good-Horses did not know him, and he said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am the son of Of-Good-Horses. My father went away and vanished." Then he was astonished, and he said: "Son, I am your father!" He became joyful, and he seated him by the fire. He said: "You are grown, and I was in sleep."

pie: owis nu eḱwobʰ(y)os (eḱwomos) ewewkʷet, "ḱēr agʰnutoi moi eḱwōns aǵontm̥ nerm̥ widn̥tei".
english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses."

pie: h₁suwékʷēs wérh₁yet kúdʰe ph₂ter sóh₂wl̥ nékʷti h₁éyti? déyḱet dʰéǵʰōm Hn̥dʰér séngʷt. sh₂wéns kʷékʷlos kʷsépi h₂én wértetor. h₂én sésti? ne sésti. h₁éyti moḱs-kʷe h₂ew mélh₃t. h₂néres swépnoy ḱéyror sóh₂wl̥ bʰebʰówdʰe. dyḗws nos spéḱyeti. nu légʰt ne-kʷe tréset. nu sh₂wéns kʷékʷlom wéydseti.
english: Of-Good-Speech said: "Father, where does the sun go at night?" He was pointing: "It sinks under the earth. There the wheel of the sun turns through the night." "Does it sleep there?" "It does not sleep. It goes, and early it comes forth again. Men lie in sleep, but the sun is alert. Sky keeps looking at us." Then he lay down, and he did not tremble in fear. Now he wants to see the wheel of the sun.

pie: owis, yesmin wl̥nā ne ēst, dedorḱe eḱwons wogʰom gʷr̥um wegʰontn̥s, bʰorom meǵHm, monum ōḱu bʰerontn̥s.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: poh₂imḗn gʰostíbʰos spélom ph₂wéni h₁épi sokʷéyet. wérh₁yet spélom moy ḱlutā́m. ph₂tḗr moy márkons h₂éǵroy péh₂st. deywós h₁ím nékʷti súpniyoy gʷémt h₂éǵt-kʷe. póh₂imen h₁éḱwōs bʰéwgonti h₁íns ph₂sdʰí. bʰéwdʰt kʷsépi-kʷe h₁éysu h₁épi sth₂éh₁yet. dyḗws gʰrémet márkōs-kʷe tr̥mént. h₁íns kapyét ne-kʷe bʰugént. h₁yód h₂wést h₁ím gʷr̥néHt. ḱl̥nwént ń̥supnōs-kʷe h₁sént.
english: By the fire a shepherd was telling a tale to the guests. He said: "Hear my tale! My father was guarding horses in the field. At night a god came to him in a dream, and he said: 'Shepherd, the horses will flee; guard them!' He woke up, and he stood by them through the night. The sky rumbled, and the horses trembled. But he held them, and they did not flee. When it grew bright, he praised him." They were listening, and they were sleepless.

pie: h₁suḱléwēs néh₂wm̥ h₂réydʰet. sn̥gʷn̥tíh₂m néh₂wm̥ nékʷti swópniyoy widéh₁yet. h₁wesuménesm̥ h₁r̥sḱét h₁ésyeh₂ey-kʷe sékʷt. h₂éǵt wédni h₁épi mē h₁éys. néh₂wm̥ gʷr̥h₃ḗti. sédt. h₂néres h₁ésyo néh₂wm̥ sl̥h₂gʷént h₁ésyeh₂i-kʷe h₁épi h₁yént. pérkʷunos gʰrémet néh₂us-kʷe séngʷt. sn̥h₂ént h₁n̥dʰént-kʷe. h₁suḱléwēs h₁wesuménesm̥ gʷr̥néHt wékʷos toy me spért. h₁ésyeh₂ey déh₃nom wédʰont.
english: Of-Good-Fame was making ready a boat. At night he was seeing in a dream the boat sinking. He went to Of-Good-Mind and told her. She said: "Do not go on the water! It will swallow the boat." He sat down. Men took his boat and went out on it. Perkʷunos roared, and the boat sank. They swam, and they came forth. Of-Good-Fame praised Of-Good-Mind: "Your word rescued me." They brought her a gift.

pie: h₃rēǵés dʰugh₂tḗr h₁suǵénh₁ēs supnóy légʰyet. h₂éwsōs h₁ésyeh₂ey wiHróm swópniyoy woydéyet. HeHḱuh₁éḱwos h₁ést Hróth₂om h₂éǵet. bʰéwdʰt h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe méh₂trey h₁íd h₂roh₁dʰéyet. méh₂tēr mléwHt só toy wiHrós h₁éseti. h₂nḗr HeHḱúbʰis h₁éḱwōys moḱs h₁ludʰét. só súpniyosyo wiHrós h₁ést. sékʷt h₃réǵ moy toy dʰugh₂térm̥ dh₃dʰí. h₁íh₂m̥ déh₃t h₁suǵénh₁ēs-kʷe h₁ím wénHt h₁íh₂m̥ lubʰyét. suHnús h₁éymos ǵn̥h₁yéto h₁ésmey-kʷe ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ dʰh₁ént.
english: The daughter of a king, Of-Good-Race, was lying down in sleep. In a dream Dawn caused her to see a man. He was swift-horsed; he was driving a chariot. She woke up and told it to her mother. The mother said: "He will be your husband." Early a man arrived with swift horses. He was the man of the dream. He said: "King, give me your daughter." He gave her, and Of-Good-Race grew fond of him; he loved her ardently. A son was born to them, and they set a famous name for him.

pie: h₁wesuménēs kl̥Héni tisr̥sú nékʷtsu légʰet. ne h₁ḗdt ne-kʷe píph₃et. nu dyḗws h₁ésyeh₂ey sh₂wéns h₁imń̥bʰis woydéyet. h₂n̥rṓm swópniyeh₂ widét. ní gʷémt nu-kʷe súpniyeh₂ wóyde. h₁íh₂m̥ gʷm̥sḱónti súpniyeh₂-kʷe wérh₁yonti. h₂roh₁dʰéyeti h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe ḱlush₁yónti. deywṓs h₁yóm woydéyonti só wóyde. h₁ésyeh₂s h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm.
english: Of-Good-Mind lay on the hill on three nights. She did not eat, and she did not drink. Then Sky caused her to see the course of the sun. She saw the dreams of men. She came down, and now she knows dreams. They come to her and tell dreams. She speaks, and they hear her. Whom the gods cause to see, that one knows. Her name is famous.

pie: nókʷts dʰǵʰémi upér ḱéyo. wiHrṓs gʷówes-kʷe swépnoy ḱóymoy h₁sént. nu h₂éwsōs diwés dʰugh₂tḗr HeHḱúns h₁éḱwons yéwgt. Hróth₂om ǵʰéyt nókʷts-kʷe bʰéwgt. h₂wést wiHrṓs-kʷe bʰudʰént. poh₂iménes gʷṓs h₂éǵrons h₂éǵont. pótnih₂es h₁íns h₂ml̥ǵént. wiHrṓs wr̥ǵyónt h₂óḱetm̥-kʷe duként. gʷéHyont h₂éwsosm̥-kʷe gʷr̥nHént. diwés dʰúgh₂ter n̥smé h₂ew gʷm̥dʰí.
english: Night was lying over the earth. Men and cattle were in sleep in the village. Then Dawn, the daughter of Sky, yoked the swift horses. She drove the chariot on, and the night fled. It became bright, and the men woke up. The shepherds drove the cattle to the pastures. The wives milked them. The men were working, and they were pulling the harrow. They sang and praised Dawn: "Daughter of Sky, come to us again!"

pie: polh₁uḱléwēs swóm dʰégʷʰontm̥ dṓm súpniyoy widéh₁yet. péh₂wr̥ h₁ím léyǵʰt. h₁gért swidyét-kʷe. h₁yéh₂ wóyde tā́m h₂usési gʷéh₂t. tósyeh₂ey súpniyom h₂roh₁dʰéyet. sékʷt péh₂wr̥ dh₂pnóm. polh₁éwes toy gʰósteyes dṓm gʷm̥yṓnti. péh₃tleh₂ mélit-kʷe h₂réydʰe. h₁íh₂ h₂réydʰet nékʷti-kʷe h₁ludʰónt. h₁édn̥t píph₃ont-kʷe h₁éy-kʷe gʷʰréh₁yet. polh₁uḱléwesos-kʷe ḱléwos h₂wékst. h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ séngʷʰont.
english: Much-Famed was seeing in a dream his own house burning. The fire was licking it. He woke up and was sweating. At dawn he went to her who knows. He told her the dream. She said: "The fire is a feast. Many guests will come to your house. Make ready the cups and the honey!" He made them ready, and in the night they arrived. They ate and drank, and it was warm. And the fame of Much-Famed grew. They were singing his name.
